output.summary: KEP-4802 adds Windows graceful node shutdown: kubelet, running as a Windows service, detects a machine shutdown or restart via the service control handler and terminates pods gracefully. The KEP is marked implementable at stage beta, with status history showing implementable from 2024-10-10.
output.rationale: Pods are not terminated gracefully when a Windows node shuts down, which can break some workloads. The KEP makes kubelet aware of the Windows shutdown event so it can run pod lifecycle termination (including pre-stop hooks) before the machine stops. Reviewers required clarifying that the feature only works when kubelet runs as a native Windows service, not under nssm.exe, and debated whether kubelet should fail to start in that case.
output.outcome_reason: Per the sources, the 1.36 enhancements team on 2026-02-11 moved the KEP to Deferred, but the stated reason is only that the owner asked for it to be deferred ("Don't worry. I will move this to `Deferred`"). The sources do not give a fuller reason. The status given to me is implementable, stage beta, so I report that and note the later deferral from the issue thread.

alternatives.option: Run kubelet as a general Windows console application
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says a general Windows application has little control over the shutdown timeout and is not reliable at receiving the shutdown event.

alternatives.option: Use the WaitToKillServiceTimeout registry key to set the shutdown timeout
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says Windows does not prefer this key for this purpose because it has a global effect on all services on the host.

alternatives.option: Keep kubelet running under nssm.exe and rely on it to forward control signals
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers said nssm.exe does not reliably pass the control signals to apps it runs, so the shutdown event would not reach kubelet.

evidence.quote: Focus on handling shutdown on machines where kubelet itself runs as a Windows service, on machines where kubelet is loaded through other loaders such as nssm.exe
General Windows application does not have much control on seting of the shutdown timeout value, and does not seem reliable to receive the shutdown event.
I don't believe nssm.exe passes the control signals to apps it runs - which is an advantage of sc.exe and needed for this scenario.
Don't worry. I will move this to `Deferred`. /remove-label tracked/yes /label tracked/no /milestone clear
